text_hash_note: text_sha256 is the hash of the whole .txt file including its notice block, so the notice block cannot quote it; body_sha256 is the hash of the converted text below the "====" line.
converter: a Python 3 RTF reader (standard library only) written for this deposit; it reads the RTF control words directly and is not part of this repository. It was validated on the Civil Liability Act 1936 (register file 1936.2267.un.rtf, version 22.6.2023) against the text already committed for that Act.
conversion: The RTF bytes are read as Latin-1 characters with the control words interpreted directly, and the hex escapes (backslash, apostrophe, two hex digits) are decoded as Windows-1252; there is no intermediate Word, HTML or PDF step.

Kept: every body paragraph in document order, including the long title, the Contents, Part and Schedule headings, section and clause headings, subsection, paragraph and subparagraph markers, definitions, tables, Note— and Example— paragraphs, and the "Table" caption line.
The (1), (a), (i) markers are tab-separated text in the RTF and stay as tabs; one paragraph is one line.
Characters: \u8212 becomes an em dash (U+2014), the RTF non-breaking hyphen becomes U+2011, and the non-breaking space (\'a0) becomes an ordinary space; no other character needed mapping.
Tables: one row per line as "| a | b |"; several paragraphs inside one cell are joined by a single space and keep their tab markers; bold and italic in cells is not carried.

Dropped: first-page, odd-page and even-page headers and footers (running heads, the "Version:" line, the footer sentence that the version is not published under the Legislation Revision and Publication Act 2002, page numbers), hyperlink field instructions (the link text is kept), bookmarks, the stylesheet, document properties, blank paragraphs, trailing spaces.

Cut: the register's "Legislative history" endnotes, which begin at the body paragraph in the RTF style leghistoryheadlevel1 and run to the end of the file: 35 paragraphs (Notes, Legislation repealed by principal Act, Legislation amended by principal Act, Principal Act and amendments, Provisions amended, Historical versions). The Contents entry "Legislative history" is left as published.
Output is UTF-8 with LF line endings.

cross_check.result: Compared on the full conversion (the legislative history included, before it was cut), as bags of words, after removing the PDF's page headers, running heads, page footers and page numbers page by page: the PDF has 11913 words and the converted text 11905. The PDF is 8 words longer, and the differences are these and no others: the first-page line "Version: 20.11.2025", the table header row "Column 1 Column 2" that the PDF reprints twice where the section 5 table continues over pages, and "s2" and "s4" in the register's own amendment tables, which the RTF spells "s 2" and "s 4". No other word differs.

notes: There is no section 2. The Contents and the body run 1, 3, 4 and so on to 60 (with 19A). The register's legislative history (not reproduced here) records "s 2 omitted under Legislation Revision and Publication Act 2002", commencement 1.1.2024. The text is reproduced as published and has not been renumbered.

Schedule 1 carries only Part 7 (clauses 24 and 25). The register's legislative history records "Sch 1 Pts 1—6 omitted under Legislation Revision and Publication Act 2002", commencement 1.1.2024. The long title is recorded there as amended under the same Act, 1.1.2024.
The latest change in the register's legislative history is section 19A, inserted by Act 55 of 2025 s 7, commencing 20.11.2025, which is the same date as the version.
The "Legislative history" endnotes were cut from the deposited text, but the Contents entry "Legislative history" remains because the Contents is reproduced as published.
The deposited text is from the unofficial RTF; the authorised PDF of the same version was used only as a cross-check.
